launcher_icon._doc: The launcher icon, generated from this declaration by 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-launcher-icons.py (pattern + category colours + glyphs in 1_cicd/src/data/launcher-icons.json). Never edit the generated res files.

name: cloud-drive
description: Diego's Cloud Drive — standalone Android storage app, lifted out of the SuperApp's Cloud▸Apps▸Drive pages so the phone's storage surface is its own icon. #609 REDESIGN over #603/#604's Compose chrome: a five-tab shell drawn by the fleet's bottom-nav island (libs:bottomnav) — Files, Volumes, Home, Sync, Configs — every tab, sub-page, place, section, filter and icon name declared in ui.* below and baked through BuildConfig. Files is a FULL X-plore-class manager over shared storage with TWO declared sections (ui.files.sections): Emulated (shared storage itself, /storage/emulated/0) and cloud-drive-storage (the ONE shared store of #575, storage.shared_root, exposed to every fleet app that holds all-files access — plain shared storage, so NO webserver is needed and libs:webserver stays deliberately unlinked); the store is seeded by DEFAULT with the public cloud repositories (storage.seed + data/drive-git-repos.json seed flags — a baked manifest with a first-run SHALLOW fetch, because an APK cannot carry a working clone). Volumes consolidates the FULL FLEET: the device's removable volumes plus every mesh mount (libs:mounts) and declared fleet connection, browse-through one tap away. Home is the drive's overview, REDESIGNED by #609 into two sections: Apps (the fleet's data-app grid, moved in from the old Apps tab) and Volumes (a snapshot of the two stores, the four volume classes, the seeded git repos' clean/dirty/ahead-behind state and the container mesh's status, each reading the SAME state the Volumes and Sync tabs render, never a second source). Sync holds three sub-pages from ONE declaration (ui.sections[sync].pages) — Git, Rclone and Mounts — moved back OUT of Configs by #609 (the mirror of #603's move the other way): the native git manager, the folder↔folder sync engine and the ftp/sftp/ssh/webdav connections. Configs keeps three sub-pages (ui.sections[configs].pages): Backups (the declared mirror/rsync jobs with cancellable progress), General (the app's settings, sign-in, storage access) and Others (removable storage, about). The four engine libraries (#567) and the ONE shared store (#575) are unchanged underneath. Dark is the default theme, set at the declaration (#336, #337). Design: a0_docs/eng-specs/cloud-drive-redesign.md. The PDF reader is the #577 native pdfium engine (build.json::pdf), the fleet's one in-process renderer, opened from the Files tab and from any app's Open-with. Build via Nix devShell, one APK out.
_doc_rsync: #1173 THE RSYNC PAGE IS FSYNC. Task #330 named Rsync without a home, #604 gave it one and #609/#1149 made it a bottom-nav page; #1173 renamed it Fsync (ui.sections[fsync], the old `rsync` id is gone) and gave it two sub-pages: Backup (engine rsync, one way, run inside the Termux guest) and Folders Sync (engine Unison, two ways, conflicts listed). It declares nothing: no rule, no job, no pair ships in the APK, the page draws what the user made and what the last runs said (see _doc_sync_rules). Configs > Backups keeps what it always was: the ON-DEVICE mirror set of data/drive-mirror-jobs.json, executed by FilesBridge.mirror().
_doc_sync_rules: #1173 data/drive-sync-rules.json ships NO folder rule and NO Unison pair (the Fsync page is real state only: the jobs and pairs the user made, kept by Cloud Account). `rules` stays an empty list so the baked SYNC_RULES_B64 and Declarations.parseSyncRules keep their shape (DeclarationsTest holds it empty); `unison` carries Unison's POLICY only (defaults, shared ignore rules) that every user pair inherits, baked as UNISON_B64.

android._doc_packaging_excludes: Duplicate META-INF files that must not reach the APK. #567 push 2 links libs:git-sync, which pulls JGit, jsch and their notices; two jars carrying the same META-INF/LICENSE fail mergeDebugJavaResource for the WHOLE app. Same block, same reason and same list as ab_cloud-libs-shared/lib-apks/build.json, which packages these very modules 36 times over. Data, not gradle, so the next collision is a one-line edit here. Never add *.kotlin_module: dropping those breaks Kotlin reflection at runtime, silently. META-INF/versions/*/OSGI-INF/MANIFEST.MF (a glob, every multi-release level): the mwiede jsch fork ships an OSGi manifest under versions/9 AND versions/15, and so do jspecify (9) and bouncycastle via sshj (15) — measured on runs 36068993994 and 36074399160, 2026-09-24. One level at a time was a chase.

storage._doc: #575 → cloud-shared-store: the store's root and its git folder (shared_root, git_subdir) are declared ONCE in ac_cloud-termux/build.json::storage + ::shared_store (owner decision 2026-10-17); this block keeps only what is cloud-drive's own: when git sync runs and how the first run seeds. app/build.gradle reads the store from there; test/test-drive-shared-store.sh fails on a second copy here.

git_sync._doc: Scheduled background sync of the repositories the user opted in (ManagedRepo.autoSync), the GitSync app's scheduler realised over WorkManager (GitSyncWorker.kt). interval_minutes is the period (WorkManager's floor is 15); require_unmetered_network keeps a push off mobile data. Same shape and same reason as release.auto_update: a build.json edit reaches installed phones through ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy.UPDATE on the next launch.

repos_source._doc: #1073 THE REPO LIST COMES FROM ONE PLACE: git-repos-master/repos.json (cloud-repos/v1). `path` is the byte copy of it that ships in this repo (refreshed by git-repos-master's ./clone.sh --sync or tools/sync-repos-sot.sh), `url` is where that registry is declared, `sha256` pins the copy. app/build.gradle BAKES the copy (REPOS_SOT_B64) and fails the build if its sha256 differs from this one, if data/drive-git-repos.json is not what tools/gen-drive-git-repos.js makes from data/drive-git-family.json + the copy, or if the family names a repo the registry lists as pending_creation or does not list. Nothing is downloaded at runtime: the APK carries the copy. test/test-drive-repos-sot.sh also compares the copy with `url` when the network answers. `ref` is the branch in the url; flip it to main once git-repos-master's claude/new-session-vb0job is merged.

seed._doc: #603 THE ONE seed declaration of the shared store. An APK cannot carry a working clone (a .git of the fleet's repositories is hundreds of megabytes and would be stale the day it shipped), so the store is seeded on FIRST RUN instead: when <shared storage>/<shared_root>/<name> does not exist for a repository data/drive-git-repos.json marks `seed: true`, StoreSeed registers it in libs:git-sync's own RepoRegistry and clones it SHALLOW (depth below) through the engine's GitEngine.clone — the same mechanism the Git sub-page's Clone button uses, never a second git. PUBLIC REPOSITORIES ONLY: a private repository needs a token this APK does not hold, so seeding one would be a clone that always fails; those stay declared-not-cloned on the Git sub-page, where the user can type a token. The manifest is the file below and nothing here restates a repository name.
seed._doc_require_unmetered_network: #730 the seed's network constraint, DECLARED like git_sync's instead of hardcoded in StoreSeed.kt. true: the first-run seed (hundreds of MB of shallow worktrees) waits for an unmetered network, so a phone set up on mobile data or a metered hotspot does not seed until it joins Wi-Fi. Until a pass runs, the Sync ▸ Git page shows the pending reason instead of nothing.

ui._doc: #868 THE NAVIGATION IS ONE DECLARATION (libs:bottomnav's NavDecl): ui.bottom_nav = the island's ids, ui.sections[] = each one's label/icon and its `pages` (the strip PageTabs draws), ui.default_section = where the app opens. Volumes' four classes, Sync's three pages and Configs' three pages are those `pages` now (they were the keys ui.volumes.classes, ui.sync.pages and ui.configs.pages; ui.tabs and ui.default_tab are gone). #603/#609 THE STRUCTURE OF THE CHROME, declared. Kotlin holds no tab list, no caption, no page list, no section list, no place list and no icon name: DriveShell renders ui.bottom_nav, SyncScreen renders ui.sections[sync].pages, ConfigsScreen renders ui.sections[configs].pages, the Files Places sheet renders ui.files.sections and ui.files.places, the Files filter pills render ui.files.filters. Every `icon` here is a name IconCatalog.kt resolves to a Material glyph; a name it does not know renders ui.icons._default and test/test-drive-shell.sh fails the build. Baked by app/build.gradle as UI_SECTIONS_B64 / UI_BOTTOM_NAV / UI_DEFAULT_SECTION / UI_SYNC_B64 / UI_FILES_B64 / UI_ICON_DEFAULT and decoded ONCE by Declarations.kt. #603 replaced #579's five tabs (files/apps/sync/backups/configs) with files/volumes/home/apps/configs, moving Sync's three pages and Backups into Configs. #609 REVERSED HALF OF THAT: Apps stopped being a tab (its grid moved into Home, ui.home below) and the freed slot is now Sync, carrying Git/Rclone/Mounts back out of Configs into their own tab — the five tabs are now files/volumes/home/sync/configs. #608 REDESIGNED THE SYNC ▸ GIT SUB-PAGE and declared it whole in ui.sync.git below: two sections (the owner's PUBLIC cloud*/front* set, which needs no login, and Personal, which signs in through libs:auth for the `repo` scope and splits the account's own listing into Public and Private), one DENSE row per repository, and fourteen per-repository operations collapsed behind each row's disclosure — every one of them a verb of libs:git-sync, force push and force pull included.

webserver._doc: Configs ▸ Webserver opens cloud-c3-webserver's own page (the Tauri app's MainActivity) through an explicit component intent: `fleet` is the app's id in the constellation fleet manifest (the package is resolved there, never typed), `activity` its launcher activity, `fallback_url` where its server answers when the app is not installed. The port is ac_cloud-c3-webserver/build.json::runtime.port; test-drive-webserver-section.sh fails when the two differ.

sections.label: Explorer
sections._doc: Owner restructure: Files is renamed Explorer and carries two sub-pages drawn by PageTabs. Local is the X-plore-class manager over shared storage and the shared store (ui.files). Cloud is the former Volumes tab, moved here whole: its four volume classes are Cloud's own sub-pages (VolumesScreen draws them per ui.volumes.sections), so Declarations.classesOf reads ui.sections[explorer].pages[cloud].pages.

sections.label: Manage
sections._doc: Owner restructure: the slot Volumes freed. Disk Management moved here from Home's sub-page and split into two sub-pages. Apps is a table of every installed app ranked by total size (StorageStatsManager behind usage access; running state and PSS from ActivityManager for this app and from the privileged shell channel, dumpsys meminfo and ps, for the rest; a dash plus a hint otherwise). Data is everything in shared storage and the shared store that is not an app, ranked by size, filtered by the groups and subtypes declared in manage/FileClassifier.kt (default: Media only; the filter persists in cloud-drive-prefs).

sections.label: Agents
sections._doc: Owner addition: on-device agents. The first, Screenshots, OCRs every screenshot and labels it with on-device ML (libs:ml-l-image's engine, detect modes text/labels/objects), incrementally, and writes the contract in data/agent-screenshots-contract.json (docs/screenshot-agent-contract.md) for other fleet apps (Cloud Tasks first).

sections.label: AI
sections._doc: Owner addition: the fleet's AI chat (libs:ai) as a tab. It talks to the fleet agent gateway (my-ai-api, mesh only) with the agent picked in the page; no token is held or read by this app (decisions-use guard D5). Declared once in libs:ai's assets/ai/ai.json; the gateway's mesh address is baked from the fleet catalogue by libs/ai/ai-gateway.gradle.

sections.label: Git
sections._doc: #1149 the former Sync > Git page is a bottom-nav page of its own with two sub-pages drawn by PageTabs. Me: sign in to the Git hosts (ui.sync.git.hosts, plus the GitHub and Cloud git ways), the signed-in account's repositories in the #1138 table with Clone when no local folder matches, and the Local Repos Parentless table (a folder holding .git whose name differs from its origin URL's basename: Rename, Rename all). Cloud: the PUBLIC cloud* repositories of the owner, listed live over GitHub REST (ui.sync.git.cloud_list) with no sign-in, with Clone. GitPageScreen dispatches on the page id, the ONE place Kotlin names them; test-drive-shell.sh diffs it against this declaration in both directions.

sections.label: Fsync
sections._doc: #1173 the former Rsync page, renamed, with two sub-pages on the second row (PageTabs, icons from libs:ui-icons): Backup = rsync, one-way mirror of a Termux-guest folder to an SSH host or another guest folder (sync/FsyncPage.kt FsyncBackupScreen, storage/BackupJobs.kt), and Folders Sync = Unison, two-way with conflict detection and keep-A / keep-B / keep-both (FolderSyncScreen over UnisonCoordinator). Everything the page draws is real state: the jobs and pairs the user made and the last result of each run; the APK declares no job, rule or pair.

sections.label: Mounts
sections._doc: #1173 the Mounts page with two sub-pages: Rclone = rclone's own `rclone config` flow in the app (backend list and option schema from `rclone config providers`, OAuth through `rclone authorize`, service account, shared drives, test with `rclone lsd`, usage with `rclone about`, edit, delete, serve over loopback WebDAV) in sync/MountsPage.kt + sync/RemoteWizard.kt, and FUSE = real FUSE mounts (rclone mount, sshfs) run inside the Termux proot guest through the CLOUD_EXEC channel, with a runtime verdict on whether FUSE can work on the device and a WebDAV serve fallback when it cannot (storage/FuseWire.kt). Remotes, keys, mounts and Unison pairs are owned by Cloud Account and reached over its accountdata door (storage/DriveCredentialsClient.kt, held to the contract by DriveCredentialsGuardTest).

sections.label: Configs
sections._doc: #603 the strip inside the Configs island — ONE declaration. #609 moved Git, Rclone and Mounts OUT into ui.sections[sync].pages above, leaving four sub-pages in the owner's order: General (#579's Configs page: storage access, sign-in, Files defaults, the declared schedule), Webserver (opens cloud-c3-webserver, ui.webserver), Backups (moved in from its own top-level tab at #603 — the declared mirror/rsync jobs with cancellable progress) and Others (removable storage, about).

files._doc_sections: #603 THE TWO SECTIONS of the Files navigator, in order, each a header in the Places sheet with the declared places that name it. `emulated` is Android shared storage itself (/storage/emulated/0); `cloud-drive-storage` is the ONE shared store of #575 (storage.shared_root), a top-level section of its own and not one place among many, because every fleet app holding all-files access reads and writes it and it is seeded by default with the PUBLIC cloud repositories (storage.seed). Removable volumes and mesh mounts are NOT here: they are the Volumes tab. The label is 'Drive store', NOT 'Cloud-Drive-Storage': the fleet's app-names guard (aa_cloud-superapp/test/test-app-names-pattern.sh T5) refuses any label that spells an application's name outside the sanctioned pattern, and 'Cloud-Drive-Storage' normalises to a prefix of cloud-drive. The section's ID still reads cloud-drive-storage, which is what this file's description names; ids are not user-facing text.
files._doc_places: The Places sheet, in order. kind: shared_root = storage.shared_root under shared storage (ALWAYS first, hero); external_root = shared storage itself; public_dir = Environment.DIRECTORY_<dir> under it; external_path = a relative path under it. A place whose folder does not exist on the device is not offered. Removable volumes, the app's slice on them and the SAF grant are discovered at runtime, not declared. The store's label is 'Shared store', never the application's name: the fleet's app-names guard (aa_cloud-superapp/test/test-app-names-pattern.sh T5) refuses any label that spells an app name the old way. #603 `section` names the ui.files.sections entry the place sits under; the sheet renders one header per declared section, in declared order.
files._doc_terminal: The Termux filesystem as a first-class root beside Emulated: Cloud Drive runs in the terminals' uid (fleet-identity.json group terminal), so it lists, copies, opens, shares and deletes there with plain file access (through CLOUD_EXEC when it is not). kind terminal_home = the terminal's $HOME (the parent of the shared store, resolved from libs:shared-store, never typed); store_path = a folder under the shared store (`path`, relative). When the shared uid is not in effect (StoreAccess.mode EXEC), the terminal's whole data dir (/data/user/<u>/<owner>, outside the store too) is listed AND changed (mkdir, new file, rename, copy, move, delete: ExecMutation) by cld.termux itself through CLOUD_EXEC, and an unreachable folder reports its real cause, never 'not a folder'.
files._doc_filters: The filter pills of a pane. An entry matches by mime (exact), mime_prefix, or extensions (lower-case, no dot); `all` has no rule and matches everything. Folders always pass a filter so the tree stays walkable.
files._doc_row_actions: #875 the actions a Files row (overflow menu), the selection bar and the current-folder crumb (tap-hold) offer, declared like the sections and filters: label and icon are what the menu prints, snack is the confirmation after the action. copy_path puts the folder's path on the clipboard through files/PathFormatter (absolute path for a local volume, content URI for a SAF volume, remote:path for an rclone mount) and the snack never echoes the path or anything secret.

icons._doc: The glyph an unknown icon name renders. IconCatalog knows this name too.

volumes._doc: #604 THE FOUR CLASSES OF VOLUME, declared, in this order. The Volumes tab used to be one list with the mesh mounts at the bottom; a volume of the fleet is one of exactly four things, so the tab is now a strip of four classes over one body — the SAME idiom as ui.sections[configs].pages (a strip inside the tab, not a stack) and the same dispatch contract: VolumesScreen's `when (classId)` is diffed against these ids in both directions by test/test-drive-shell.sh. Cloud-Constellation is the on-device mesh between OUR same-signature fleet apps (data/drive-constellation.json); Cloud-Containers is the fleet's container volume mounts, which is exactly what MountsSyncScreen already drew (data/drive-connections.json entries with machine=container); Cloud-Machines is the same declaration filtered to the HOST-level entries, grouped by machine_kinds; S3 is the rclone remotes whose type is in s3_remote_types, browsed through `rclone lsjson`. The device's own removable volumes stay a header ABOVE the strip: they are discovered at runtime (Places.discovered), never declared, and #603's capability is not lost. #613 REGROUPS the four classes into TWO sections declared in `sections` below — Cloud Constellation (the mesh/cloud side, the fleet's own volumes) and Personal Mounts (Machines, Containers, S3, carrying a sign-in affordance that deep-links to cloud-sa's Profile) — a pure reparent: the classes, their dispatch and their filters are unchanged.
volumes._doc_sections: #613/#630 THE TWO SECTIONS the four classes regroup into, in render order. `classes` names the ui.sections[volumes].pages ids each section owns. #630 RENAMED them to the owner's own words — Fleet Volumes and Personal Volumes — and, more importantly, fixed what they LOOKED like: #613 stacked both pill strips at the top of ONE shared body, so two declared sections rendered as one list and the owner reported 'SEPARATE TWO SECTIONS!! IS TWO SECTIONS!!'. Each section now owns its OWN header, its OWN pill strip, its OWN selected class and its OWN rows underneath, and the bodies split the screen; test/test-drive-volumes-sections.sh fails the build on a single shared body. `auth: true` gives the section the Personal-Volumes sign-in affordance below (personal_auth), a deep-link to the fleet's auth Profile; Fleet Volumes is the mesh/cloud side and carries none. A class no section names is NOT lost: it gets an 'Others' section of its own (the #292 rule — never lose a row). The union of every section's `classes` must cover ui.sections[volumes].pages; test/test-drive-shell.sh D13 holds it so.
volumes._doc_personal_auth: #613 THE AUTH AFFORDANCE of the Personal Mounts section — a LINK, not a second auth surface. The sign-in that holds the SSH keys and the Authelia web-auth flow is the fleet's ONE auth (libs:auth), hosted by cloud-sa's Profile ▸ Connect; this deep-links there rather than reimplementing it here. `fleet` resolves to a package at build time from the SAME constellation manifest the Apps grid uses (no second package list); the launch intent carries `target` as the string extra named by `extra`, which is the fleet's launcher-shortcut deep-link contract (cloud-sa ShellActivity.handleShortcutIntent → onTileClicked resolves page:config/profile), so the tap lands on Profile ▸ Connect. If cloud-sa is not installed the affordance reports it and does nothing else.
volumes._doc_machine_kinds: The host classes Cloud-Machines groups by, in render order; a declared connection's `machine` field names one of these or `container` (the default, which belongs to Cloud-Containers instead). A kind with no connection renders an honest empty group, never a hidden one.
volumes._doc_s3_remote_types: The data/drive-remotes.json `type` values Cloud-Constellation's sibling S3 class owns: Oracle Object Storage buckets (s3) and Google Drive / Workspace (google-drive). The spelling is the one that file uses, not rclone's own internal type, because this filters the DECLARATION.
volumes._doc_constellation_path: #604/#630 WHERE ONE FLEET APP'S FOLDER IS ACTUALLY READABLE FROM ANOTHER. This used to be /storage/emulated/0/Android/data/<package>/files, and that path CAN NEVER BE OPENED by cloud-drive: since Android 11 (API 30) /Android/data/<pkg>/ is readable only by its owning app, MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE does NOT grant it (Android/data and Android/obb are explicitly carved out of that permission), and Android 13+ blocks the SAF/DocumentsProvider route into those trees as well. The device is API 35, so every row read 'Not verifiable: cannot read <package>' and its Open did nothing — the OS refusing correctly. It is now a leg of the ONE SHARED STORE (storage.shared_root, resolved through SharedStore.resolve so the absolute path is still written down nowhere): a location the FLEET controls and that every app holding all-files access can genuinely reach. The <package> placeholder is substituted with the resolved package id, once.
volumes._doc_constellation_owner_only: #630 THE PLATFORM WALL, DECLARED, so no row can offer a path that is guaranteed to fail. `path` is the app's own Android/data folder; `openable: false` says cloud-drive must never render an Open affordance onto it; `blocked_since_sdk` is the API level that carved it out of every other app's reach; `handoff: true` says the row offers 'Open in <app>' instead — a launch of the OWNING app, which is the one process that can read that directory. The row states the reason in plain words rather than rendering 'Not verifiable' as a mystery, which is the #292 rule applied to a platform refusal: never an empty box, and never a button that cannot work.

sync._doc_cloud_list: #1149 Sync > Git > Cloud: the PUBLIC cloud* repositories of `owner`, listed live over the GitHub REST route `path` (api base: ui.sync.git.api.base_url) with NO credential, then filtered to public repositories whose name starts with `name_prefix`. CloudRepos.filter is the rule; when the network refuses, the page shows the declared public_repos set and says so.
sync._doc_git_hosts: #1149 Sync > Git > Me: the hosts beyond the GitHub and Cloud-git ways, in render order. `kind` picks the listing parser and the auth header (GitHosts: gitlab, gitea for Codeberg and any Gitea-compatible host, bitbucket, azure). The credential is a personal access token (an app password for Bitbucket) the user pastes, kept in libs:git-sync's GitCredentialStore (SafeEncryptedPrefs): no OAuth client is registered for this app and none is invented. `needs_user` asks for a user name (Azure DevOps: the organisation, substituted for {user} in api_base); `clone_user` is the HTTPS user a clone presents when the host fixes one. The self-hosted Cloud Gitea keeps its own way (ui.sync.git.ways, the fleet rung).
sync._doc_git: #608 THE SYNC ▸ GIT PAGE, declared whole. Kotlin holds no section title, no repository name, no owner, no GitHub endpoint, no operation label and no remote-URL shape: GitReposScreen renders THIS block and libs:git-sync performs every verb it names. The page is DATA-DENSE on purpose — one compact row per repository so a long list is scannable, with the per-repository operations collapsed behind the row's own disclosure (ops below) instead of a large box each. TWO SECTIONS, in `sections` order. `public` needs NO login: it is the declared set of the owner's PUBLIC repositories in the `name_families` name families, cloned over plain HTTPS, and `public_repos` below is that set. `personal` shows `login_ways` until a sign-in lands and then splits the AUTHENTICATED listing into `personal_groups` (Public, then Private), each alphabetical by name — nothing of the owner's account is declared here, because a private repository list is not a fact a build can hold. Every clone lands in storage.shared_root's git folder (storage.git_subdir), never an app-private or exec volume.

git._doc_sections: The two sections of the page, in render order. `login_required` says whether the section has anything to show before a sign-in: the public set is declared and always rendered, the personal section renders its login control and nothing else until one lands. GitReposScreen's `when (section.id)` is diffed against these ids in both directions by test/test-drive-git-page.sh.
git._doc_personal_groups: How the authenticated listing is split, in render order. The group a repository falls into is the API's own `private` flag, never a guess and never a declaration: a repository that goes private between two builds moves group by itself.
git._doc_ways: #684 THE TWO PARALLEL, ALWAYS-VISIBLE WAYS into the personal section, in render order — the owner rejected the one-chain-one-affordance shape where whichever rung answered took the section over. Each way is its own card: its own large sign-in button, its own status light and one-line state, its own repository listing below it, and rows that clone FROM the leg that listed them. `rung` names an auth.git_chain rung of ab_cloud-libs-shared/build.json; the rung's KIND is the only thing GitReposScreen dispatches on (fleet_proxy ⇒ Authelia session, listing and in-process clone on that session — f45bbbe31's engine; gh_on_device ⇒ gh itself (#689): gh's own `auth login`, `gh repo list` split public/private by gh's isPrivate, and an in-process clone on the credential gh holds; with gh signed out, the #629 vault credential still lists over REST with no tap). Neither card gates, hides or replaces the other: both can be signed in at once and both lists can show at once. The declared chain (auth.git_chain.order) STAYS as the automatic no-tap resolution order and for gh/gix credential resolution; what this changes is the PAGE. A way naming a rung the chain does not declare renders its card with the one line that says so, never a placeholder; a way with no rung is dropped at parse. The Cloud git sign-in rides the fleet's own browser (auth.browser_mission, which captures the session cookie) and says so when it falls back to the in-app dialog; the GitHub sign-in is gh's own device flow, whose code the card shows and copies.
git._doc_login_ways: #641 THE ONE way into the personal section, plus the user's own key. The `webauth` way is GONE: it drove an OAuth 2.0 device grant against a GitHub APP client, and GitHub Apps ship with Device Flow OFF, so every press of Start ended in `device_flow_disabled`. The HTTPS credential is the one the vault config import delivers (auth.applies.git.credential_id, #629) and there is no browser login to fall back to - a browser one would need a GitHub OAuth App of the fleet's own, which #689 rules out for good (test-drive-git-gh-leg.sh): the GitHub card signs in with gh's own `auth login` instead. `ssh_key` is the user's EXISTING key: the path and passphrase libs:git-sync's ManagedRepo/GitCredentialStore already hold (sync_auth_key_path on the per-repo sheet), used as GitAuth.Ssh - no second key mechanism is built here, and SSH cannot list an account, so that way clones only.
git._doc_api: Where the authenticated listing comes from. `repos_path` is the affiliation=owner page of the REST list-your-repositories route, paged to `max_pages` × per_page so a large account is not silently truncated to its first page; `web_url` is the row's open-on-web link. `{owner}` and `{name}` are the only placeholders, substituted once by Declarations.
git._doc_terminal: #642 GIT IS THE TERMINAL'S JOB, NOT THIS APP'S. cloud-drive holds no git credential and mints none: a clone is handed to cloud-terminal-nix, which already carries a real git CLI inside its proot rootfs and the credential that pushes all day. That is why `webauth` did not need replacing with a second login (#641 deleted an OAuth device grant against a GitHub App that could never work) -- the fleet already owns this operation, and the app that owns it is the one that should run it. THE PIPE IS NOT NEW: RunCommandService is ours (ac_cloud-nix-on-droid RunCommandService.java), its action and permission are declared in that app's manifest, and #198/#620 exist precisely to make it usable from another app (allow-external-apps=true, rewritten on every launch and boot). cloud-drive is its first in-app client. `fleet` is resolved to a package at BUILD time from the same constellation manifest the Apps grid and ui.volumes.personal_auth resolve against, and every {package} below is substituted from it once -- so the terminal's id is written down here exactly as often as it is written down anywhere else: once. `command` is bin/login rather than a store path: login execs the caller's argv inside the proot where git and its glibc loader exist (the argv branch #641 fixed and tests), so `login git clone <url> <dest>` is a real git in a real rootfs, while exec'ing a /nix/store binary straight from Android would die for want of an interpreter. background=false so the clone runs in a visible session the user can read, including git's own error text. #669/#689 THE TWO IN-PROCESS EXCEPTIONS, for one reason: the terminal's git can present neither credential. A row the fleet listed clones on the Authelia session (#669); a row gh listed clones on the credential gh holds, asked through gh's own git-credential helper (the terminals declare no git credential helper and carry no gh on their PATH).

terminal._doc_ops: The argv handed to bin/login, per operation. {url} and {dest} are the only placeholders and are substituted once, positionally, never concatenated into a shell string -- an argv array cannot be re-split by a space or a quote in a repository name.

git._doc_remote_modes: What a row's Remote operation can switch `origin` to, in order. One URL shape each, declared, so the page never composes a remote by hand: HTTPS (what a token authenticates), SSH (what the user's key authenticates) and read-only, which is the same HTTPS URL with `read_only` set — the page then refuses push and force push on that repository rather than offering a button that always fails.
git._doc_ops: THE OPERATIONS of one cloned repository, in the order the row's disclosure lays them out. Every id is a verb of libs:git-sync's GitEngine or a read of the clone on disk — fetch/pull/commit/push/force_push/force_pull/history/remote go through the engine (force_push and force_pull are #608's additions to it, each destructive on exactly ONE side, which is why both carry `destructive` and the row asks first), while metadata/stats/hooks/actions/size are reads of the working tree. GitReposScreen's `when (opId)` is diffed against these ids in both directions, so an operation declared without a handler — or a handler with no declared operation — fails test/test-drive-git-page.sh.
git._doc_status: #850 THE ONE STATUS READER (sync/GitStatusReader.kt). Every repository's status is read on its own thread, awaited for at most timeout_seconds (then the row says error(timeout) instead of 'reading…' for ever), at most concurrency at once so a large clone never holds the others back, and cached for ttl_seconds so re-entering the page does not re-walk every tree.
git._doc_auto_pull: #850 'Auto pull on open': when on, opening Sync ▸ Git pulls every cloned repository (a plain pull, never the destructive force pull) on the ONE declared credential path (#818). default_on is the setting before the owner touches the toggle (then persisted per device); require_unmetered_network = Wi-Fi only, like git_sync and the seed.
git._doc_public_repos: #608 THE DECLARED PUBLIC SET of the `public` section, alphabetical by name. DERIVED, not hand-picked: every repository of `owner` whose name begins with one of `name_families` AND whose GitHub `private` flag is false, enumerated once over the REST list route and verified one by one (an unauthenticated GET of /repos/<owner>/<name> answering 200 IS the proof of public). cloud-u-android — this repository — is in the set; it was missing from data/drive-git-repos.json's curated family's intent and is named here explicitly for that reason. front-data is HERE and PUBLIC: drive-git-repos.json marked it private, which the live API contradicts, and that file is corrected in the same change. There is no repository called `front`: the front-end tree of this fleet is `ffront`, carried as its OWN name family (the `front` family does not match it) and seeded like the cloud set, so it is present here explicitly rather than silently renamed. #616 CORRECTED THE SET: the seed set is what cloud/repos.json and ffront/repos.json DECLARE public, not a name prefix, so it grew diegonmarcos.github.io and front-diegonmarcos — both are HERE now, `diegonmarcos` joining the name families for the first of them, because a repository that seeds into the store and is missing from the page is a store the page cannot show (P2 refuses that disagreement). NOT in the set, on purpose: git-repos-master (public, but outside the name families) and every cloud*/front* repository whose flag is private (cloud-data, cloud-data-lfs, cloud-me-my-ai, cloud-me, cloud-me_configs, cloud-me_data-private, cloud-me_vault, cloud-notes, front-galaxy-gaia, front-unity) — those reach the page through the personal section's authenticated listing, which is where a private repository belongs. THE FIELDS ARE `repo` AND `caption`, NOT `name`/`label`, and that is not cosmetic: the fleet's app-names guard (aa_cloud-superapp/test/test-app-names-pattern.sh T5) sweeps every `name`, `label` and `title` in every build.json and refuses a value that normalises onto an application's name — `cloud-me_data-pub` normalises onto the cloud-me application — and it is RIGHT to refuse an application name written that way. A git repository name is a different kind of fact from an application name, so it is carried under a key that says which one it is, instead of dropping a repository out of a set whose whole point is to be complete.

pdf._doc: #577 THE ONE PDF ENGINE declaration. cloud-drive is the fleet's PDF reader (#458) and its reader is the only in-process PDF renderer in the fleet (#463): every other app reaches it through the Android manifest (an ACTION_VIEW application/pdf chooser), never by carrying a renderer. app/build.gradle reads this block and adds the dependency, so the pin lives in data, not in a gradle string; test/test-drive-pdf-engine.sh holds the app's source to it (the only file that names the library is PdfEngine.kt).

engine._doc_artifacts: BOTH, on the compile classpath. The binding's Gradle metadata publishes pdfiumandroid-core (the JNI half, where the .so files live) as a RUNTIME-only dependency, but the public constructor PdfiumCore(context, config, coreInternal: PdfiumCoreU = ...) names a class from it, so the Kotlin compiler cannot compile a bare PdfiumCore(context) without it (found reading pdfiumandroid-2.0.0.module and PdfiumCore.kt, not by building: there is no build here). pdfiumandroid-api (models, FindFlags, PdfPasswordException) arrives transitively.
engine._doc_version: PINNED ON PURPOSE BELOW THE LATEST (2.0.3, 3.0.x-alpha). 2.0.1 and later publish against kotlin-stdlib 2.4, and this repo compiles with Kotlin 2.3.20 (root build.gradle): a Kotlin compiler reads class metadata one minor version ahead at most, so 2.0.1+ would fail to compile here. 2.0.0 is a stable release built with Kotlin 2.3.10, read from the sources jar and the AARs on Maven Central, not from memory. Raise it together with the root Kotlin plugin version, never alone.
engine._doc_licence: The binding is Apache-2.0 (its LICENSE; the pom declares the same). The native engine inside it, PDFium, is BSD-3-Clause (pdfium.googlesource.com LICENSE). Both permissive: nothing copyleft reaches the APK and nothing is vendored into this repository, which is what 1_cicd/src/data/licence-boundaries.json guards (mixed-licence upstreams whose restricted directories must stay out). It is a Maven Central dependency, not a source tree.
engine._doc_native_abis: What the AAR ships (libpdfium.so + libpdfiumandroid.so per ABI, ~5 MB for arm64-v8a). android.abi_filters still decides which of them reach an APK.

signing._doc: ONE shared Cloud-constellation signing key for ALL Android apps. KEY LOCATION: A_A0-Providers/D_TOOLS-DEVICES/d2-android/release.jks (OU=Cloud Constellation) + A_A0-Providers/D_TOOLS-DEVICES/d2-android/signing.secrets.yaml.

diagnostics._doc_debug_api: #669 the loopback debug/test API for the Sync▸Git flow. NO new server: libs:devtools' AppDebugServer (linked via libs:core, started by its DebugInitProvider) binds this package's own 127.0.0.1 port from libs/devtools/debug-ports.json (#792; it was the first free port in 38090-38139, which ran out) and gates every route except /api/system/ping behind the fleet's one Bearer token (SuperApp mints it, siblings adopt it; the unauthorized banner proves liveness). This app registers its own route groups on it from debugapi/DriveDebugApi.kt (via DriveDebugApiProvider, the same pre-Application init trick): GET /api/health (version_code + store root), GET /api/git/state (registered repos with remote HOST only + fleet-session presence as a boolean), POST /api/git/chain (the real DriveGitChain.resolve; narrative + answeredBy, never a token), POST /api/git/list?rung= (the real DriveGitChain.repos, dispatched on the rung's declared kind: gh repo list in the gh engine for the github rung, FleetGit.repos for a fleet rung; names/owners, no URLs), POST /api/git/clone?name=&url= (the page's own GitSyncCoordinator.cloneInto, waited on for the engine's real outcome; a fleet-listed URL rides the fleet session, any other presents the github rung's credential, which asks the gh engine first), POST /api/session?cookie= (injects a fleet session into process memory; answers a boolean, never echoes), GET /api/log/tail?lines=N (tail of Download/<debug_log_dir>/). #741 GET /api/net/resolve?host= and /api/net/dns (Android's resolver for this app's uid, the same lookup the rclone tunnel makes, and the upstreams it is answered by) are NOT this app's: #758 moved them into AppDebugServer itself, so every app linking libs:core serves them and this list names only Drive's own groups. No token, cookie or Authorization value is ever returned or logged; test/test-drive-debug-api.sh mutation-proves the bind, the gate, the no-secret rule and that the clone route reuses the page's path.
diagnostics._doc_debug_log_dir: The Download/ subfolder DriveDebugLog writes the app's own on-device debug log into, same family as the superapp's Download/superapp-logs/. Declared here (baked as BuildConfig.DEBUG_LOG_DIR by app/build.gradle) so the folder name lives in data, never in Kotlin. The log carries the git flow's decision points — clone start/result, sync outcomes, seed outcomes — with UTC timestamps and an explicit Z offset, because a local-time log read from a UTC shell has been misread as stale before. Readable off the phone with no adb: any file manager or Termux (~/storage/Download).

auth._doc: #587 What a sign-in through Configs > Sign in (libs:auth, the fleet's ONE sign-in module) yields for THIS app. The artifact is the same consolidated document the superapp fetches (/pub/superapp/config/<user>, or the vault bundle); this app applies only the sections named here, and says so per section instead of writing a blob. `git.github_token` is the credential the shared store's clone/push needs: it is stored in libs:git-sync's keystore-backed GitCredentialStore for every managed repository whose auth is https, and repointed on every later sign-in. `rclone.remotes` are rclone.conf sections (name -> type + options) merged through RcloneConfig.upsert - declared here because a remote's secret is what a drive sign-in should bring; the artifact does not carry the section yet (no host emits it), and the apply reports that absence instead of pretending. Nothing else in the artifact (WireGuard keys, mail passwords, AI tokens) is this app's to write.

git.into: git-sync credential store, every managed https repository AND the credential_id below
git._doc_credential_id: #629 THE VAULT IS THE PRIMARY GIT CREDENTIAL PATH, and this is the id it is held under. `into` above only ever reached repositories that were ALREADY cloned, so on a fresh phone a vault import wrote the token nowhere and Sync ▸ Git still demanded a browser login through a GitHub device flow the provider has switched OFF (`device_flow_disabled`) — a browser ceremony for a credential the vault had already delivered. The SAME keystore-backed GitCredentialStore (libs:git-sync; there is no second credential store anywhere) now also holds the token under this declared id, so the account listing and a clone of a repository that does not exist on the phone yet both work straight after the import. The export really does carry it: cloud-vault C_A1-configs/git/sources.json declares git.github_token and the emitted profile-secrets.json holds a live token. The device grant stays as the FALLBACK for a phone with no vault import, and ab_cloud-libs-shared/build.json::auth.grant_remedies makes its provider-side failure say so.

engines._doc: #705 ENGINES THIS APP BINDS INSTEAD OF COMPILING. Each is a Cloud-Lib-*.apk the Store installs (a fleet row of kind lib) whose service answers core's IDataBackend; this app links nothing of the engine's module, so an engine change republishes that one APK and not this app. Per engine: `fleet` is its Store row in aa_cloud-superapp/data/constellation-fleet.json, from which app/build.gradle resolves the package (an id the manifest lacks fails the build — no package is typed here or in Kotlin); `action` finds the service inside that package ({package} is substituted at build time and matches the engine manifest's ${applicationId}.ENGINE); `min_contract` is the lowest engine CONTRACT (meta-data on the engine's service) that answers every method this app calls — the client reads it through PackageManager BEFORE binding, so an engine too old to serve this build is named as such instead of failing a call; `login_poll_ms` / `login_max_ms` pace the one long call, gh's device-flow sign-in, which the engine runs on its own thread and the client polls rather than holding a binder thread for minutes (gh's own code expires after 15).

modules._doc: Single source of truth for the Gradle module graph. settings.gradle iterates this list.

libs:shizuku-adb-debug-tools._doc_dir: Manage ▸ Apps reads running state and RAM of OTHER apps through the fleet's privileged shell (ps -A -o NAME, dumpsys meminfo): Android 5.1+ shows an app only its own processes. Shared BY REFERENCE; build.json::shizuku_client puts the SuperApp bridge first.

libs:core._doc_dir: Shared BY REFERENCE from aa_cloud-superapp/libs/ — settings.gradle points projectDir here instead of at a local copy. Every app used to carry its own copy-pasted tree and they drifted: 6 apps sat 228 source lines behind superapp's updater. One directory, no sync step, no drift.

libs:databackend._doc_dir: #825 the engine wire (IDataBackend + DataBackendClient/Service), out of libs:core so a wire edit rebuilds only the engines and the apps that bind one.

libs:devtools._doc_dir: Shared BY REFERENCE from aa_cloud-superapp/libs/, same as libs:core. Not listed in app.depends_on and not linked in app/build.gradle: libs:core pulls it in with an `api` dependency, which is what gives every app the constellation-wide debug API (127.0.0.1:38090+, own-process logcat) without per-app wiring that would drift.

libs:crash._doc: #1122 libs:core `api`s this module (the default crash handler, the local crash sink and the generic crash screen); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path and the ship workflow's path triggers see it, not linked in the app's own gradle.

libs:fleetconfig-model._doc: #873 libs:core `api`s this module (the setup provider every app serves, describe / export / apply / status); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path and the ship workflow's path triggers see it, not linked in the app's own gradle.

libs:updater._doc_dir: Shared BY REFERENCE from aa_cloud-superapp/libs/ — settings.gradle points projectDir here instead of at a local copy. Every app used to carry its own copy-pasted tree and they drifted: 6 apps sat 228 source lines behind superapp's updater. One directory, no sync step, no drift.

libs:ml-l-image._doc_dir: THE shared scan engine (task #459/#460): ZXing barcode decode + ML Kit text-recognition + typed-payload parsing, shared BY REFERENCE the same way libs:core and libs:updater are. cloud-media-center consumes the SAME directory — one engine, two apps, no private copy to drift.

modules._doc_engines: #567 THE FOUR ENGINE LIBRARIES. The owner's vision for this application: the main APK is CHROME, and every tooling is a full engine in its OWN library — libs:file-editor (the full text editor), libs:git-sync (the native git manager that finishes the #437/#448 GitSync story: status, stage/unstage, commit, push/pull, branch list, log, diff, remotes, conflicts — GitSync's UX, over JGit), libs:rclone (remotes config + declared/ad-hoc sync jobs with progress + remote browsing, over a sha256-pinned static rclone binary) and libs:mounts (ftp/sftp/ssh/webdav connections with browse-through). Each lives on the shared shelf and is shared BY REFERENCE like every other module here, so lib-apks also ships each one as cloud-lib-{name}. THE MODULE BOUNDARY IS LAW: a library imports nothing from any application (test/test-drive-engine-modules.sh fails on the first lib -> app import). Compose only (#565): each exports ONE @Composable screen that this app's EngineActivity hosts (push 5). Landed as independently green pushes — (1) skeletons + declarations, (2) git-sync, (3) file-editor, (4) rclone + mounts, (5) drive wiring — so a module on main is never half-wired: until its engine push lands, a skeleton renders its own title and nothing else, and the app does not route to it.

libs:git-sync._doc_dir: Engine library #567 push 2: the native git manager. Lives on the shelf beside the vendored Flutter GitSync tree (libs/gitsync, GPL-3.0) whose UI could not be embedded; this module is the Kotlin/Compose realisation of that UX over JGit.

libs:file-editor._doc_dir: Engine library #567 push 3: the full text editor that replaces the in-page textarea editor of #302 for anything beyond a quick edit.

libs:shared-store._doc_dir: cloud-shared-store's store-access layer (contract): where the store is, whether the shared uid is in effect (DIRECT) or git/rclone must run inside cld.termux through CLOUD_EXEC (EXEC), and the legacy-path migration rule. Shared BY REFERENCE; reads ac_cloud-termux/build.json::shared_store.

libs:rclone._doc_dir: Engine library #567 push 4: rclone remotes + jobs + progress. The declared jobs stay in this app's data/drive-rclone-jobs.json and data/drive-remotes.json; the library receives them as models, never reads them itself.

libs:sysdns._doc_dir: #741 Not an engine and not linked by the app: libs:rclone compiles it, so settings.gradle must include it. It is how the bundled rclone binary resolves a remote's name inside this app, through Android's resolver and therefore the SuperApp's DNS menu (ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs/sysdns/data/sysdns.json::_doc).

libs:mounts._doc_dir: Engine library #567 push 4: ftp / sftp / ssh / webdav mounts with browse-through. Declared fleet connections stay in data/drive-connections.json; the library receives them as models.

libs:auth._doc_dir: #587 THE sign-in of the fleet, the SAME module cloud-superapp's Profile > Connect hosts, shared BY REFERENCE like every module here: Configs > Sign in offers the four declared ways (Authelia bearer, Authelia web-auth, GitHub, Google) from ONE declaration (ab_cloud-libs-shared/build.json::auth) and hands this app the consolidated artifact; DriveAuthApply then writes only the DRIVE-relevant sections (auth.applies below).

libs:nav-bar-bottom._doc: #1154 shared navigation and theme design, shared BY REFERENCE.

libs:nav-bar-top-first-row._doc: #1154 shared navigation and theme design, shared BY REFERENCE.

libs:nav-bar-top-second-row._doc: #1154 shared navigation and theme design, shared BY REFERENCE.

libs:theme-background._doc: #1154 shared navigation and theme design, shared BY REFERENCE.

libs:bottomnav._doc_dir: #579 THE fleet bottom-nav island (#565): the five tabs are drawn by the same Compose declaration superapp, mail, wallet and me render — one geometry, one pill, one collapse rule. Shared BY REFERENCE like every other module here.

libs:ui-icons._doc: #1160 the nav icon catalog (name to ImageVector, tinted or brand): every nav glyph of every app, shared BY REFERENCE; libs:bottomnav depends on it.

libs:disk._doc_dir: #813 THE Disk Management engine: volumes, storage map, huge files, duplicates, per-app sizes, cache/temp clean and memory behind DiskEngine (contract DiskContract.VERSION), rendered by home/DiskScreen.kt and answered on /api/disk/*. #763 class pinned (1_cicd/src/data/lib-classes.json): it reads and deletes under THIS app's grants (usage access, all-files access), so it is compiled in here and ships no APK of its own.

libs:ai._doc_dir: The AI tab: the fleet's AI chat (libs:ai) over the fleet agent gateway (my-ai-api, mesh only). Shared BY REFERENCE. This app holds no OpenRouter token and reads none (decisions-use guard D5): the gateway holds the fleet key. Its mesh address is baked as BuildConfig.AI_GATEWAY_URL by libs/ai/ai-gateway.gradle.

libs:model-catalogue._doc_dir: libs:ai's `api` dependency: the shared agent descriptor (assets/agents/agents.json) its Agent picker lists. Listed so settings.gradle resolves the path.

libs:disk-scan._doc_dir: #813 libs:disk's arithmetic (walk, storage map, huge-file threshold, duplicates, clean plan), plain JVM, PIT-gated at 80. Not linked by the app: libs:disk compiles it with `api`, so settings.gradle must include it.

modules._doc_git_chain_libs: #646 the git auth+ops chain's two pinned static binaries, libs:gh and libs:gix, are NOT linked here any more. #705: gh runs in Cloud-Lib-Gh.apk's own process and this app binds it (engines.gh); gix was linked and called by nothing, so it ships only as Cloud-Lib-Gix.apk. A change to either republishes that one lib APK and not this app; their build-time refusals and gix's clone/fetch-only verbs are checked where they ship (ab_cloud-libs-shared/lib-apks/test/test-git-binaries.sh). packaging.jniLibs.useLegacyPackaging stays on for libs:rclone's binary.
modules._doc_engine_flag: #579 `engine: true` marks a module as one of the FOUR ENGINE LIBRARIES (the host contract: one @Composable <X>Screen(target, onOpenFile, onClose), a title string, the module boundary). Until #579 every Compose library this app linked WAS an engine, so test-drive-engine-modules.sh discovered engines as 'Compose library'; libs:bottomnav (the fleet's nav island, chrome not tooling) is the first Compose library here that is not one, so the role is now declared, not inferred.

web._doc: #876 Cloud Drive as a Kotlin/Wasm page (web/ is its own gradle root; the shared libs' pure-Compose sources arrive through the ab_cloud-libs-shared/web composite). Rendered into 1_cicd/src/cicd/ship-cloud-drive-wasm.yml by the workflow generator: `./gradlew wasmJsBrowserDistribution` in `dir`, tested by test/test-drive-web.sh, `build/dist/wasmJs/productionExecutable` zipped to `artifact` and attached to the rolling release as `gh_asset`. A mocked page: the island and tab strips are ui.bottom_nav / ui.sections as the Android shell reads them, the first section shows mock data and the rest say they live in the Android app. The APK's own ship ignores this directory.

tests._doc: Read by 1_cicd/dist/scripts/cloud-android-test-engine.sh, which the ship workflow runs before it builds. Until #330 this block was absent and test/ did not exist, so the shell phase printed COVERAGE-GAP and exited 0: the only question this application's pipeline asked was whether Gradle exited 0, and Gradle cannot see a WebView calling a Kotlin class by string name.

shell._doc_requires: A tester that shells out to a tool which is not installed does not fail — it returns a verdict from the tool's ABSENCE. Listing them here makes a missing one fatal at the engine's preflight instead of a green tick over assertions that never ran.

unit._doc: Runs gradle test (build.sh test — the app's documented 'gradle test (JVM unit tests)' step) on every ship. #579 the app module now carries its own JVM suite (app/src/test: the Files state reducers, the archive path model, the transfer/rename plans, the Zip-Slip guard, the sync history and the per-repo schedule decision, the declarations, and a Robolectric Compose layout-tree test of the shell and the Files pane). The module graph also includes :libs:ml-l-image, whose typed-payload parser suite lives in this app's unit phase on purpose, and the four engine libraries' suites. #577 adds PdfConvertTest and PdfLayoutTest, which run the PDF converter and the reader's page layout as real code on the CI runner.

auto_update._doc_max_installs_per_pass: Most install sessions ONE unattended background pass may open. A background pass cannot show the system install dialog (Android 10+ blocks background activity starts), so each install it starts leaves a tap-to-install notification holding a PackageInstaller session until the user answers it. Unbounded, one pass over the 40-entry fleet opens 40 and the installer hits Android's 50-session cap - 'Too many active sessions for UID'. The remainder is picked up by the next pass. User-initiated 'Update all' is NOT capped: it runs in the foreground where the dialog appears and sessions resolve at once.

analytics._doc: Consumed by :libs:analytics, which reads THIS file (rootDir) at build time and bakes the values into BuildConfig. Both backends are single-site today, so every app reports into the same site and is told apart by .app — give each app its own site_id once per-app sites exist in Umami/Matomo.

shizuku_client._doc: Cloud Drive is a shell CLIENT (Manage ▸ Apps: ps + dumpsys meminfo), never a server owner: the ladder tries the SuperApp's privilege plane first, then stock Shizuku. No rish here.

privileged_channel._doc: What THIS app declares it needs the privileged shell channel for (see ac_cloud-store/build.json::privileged_channel). Listed, as written, in the Declared needs section of the ADB Shell page (Configs > Others).

needs.label: Running apps and RAM

_doc_fleet_agents: This app's agents, in the fleet agent registry's one shape (aa_cloud-superapp/build.json::_doc_fleet_agents). Consolidated into aa_cloud-superapp/data/fleet-agents.json by 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-fleet-agents.py and shown in Cloud SuperApp ▸ Configs ▸ Apps ▸ Agents ▸ Fleet agents.

fleet_agents.name: Screenshot agent
fleet_agents.summary: OCRs and labels every screenshot on the phone with on-device ML and writes the contract in data/agent-screenshots-contract.json.
